language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Welcome divers! I’m Sam. I’ve been waiting for you here at the coral reef. Coral reefs provide a habitat, or in other words a home, for a variety of fish and other animals.
This coral reef is in the Caribbean Sea. Close to the shore are the mangrove forests in the shallow sea water that provide nesting habitat for the sea birds.
Seagrass meadows are places where manatees live and where young turtles are nursed. Dive out farther and explore the coral reefs – a habitat that many organisms share.

Factors like food, sunlight, water, and shelter make a habitat. Many organisms on the reef are sharing and helping each other survive. Even predators serve an important function by removing sick fish.

Other factors impact the habitat too: Pollution has removed the minerals that shellfish and coral need to make their hard shells, and low oxygen in the water is killing the coral. When coral dies, all the animals that depend on it are in danger of losing their homes.
I'm going to explore all the different organisms and their habitat at the bottom of the sea. Are you coming along?
Are you ready to get your feet wet? Dive in! Let’s get started!

As a home for many plants and animals, the coral reef can be a fragile habitat. Many factors can influence it for good and have a positive impact on the organisms that live there. But there are also factors that can have a bad or negative impact on the coral reef. Can you identify if each factor has a positive or negative impact on the habitat?
